title: Selector pack
description: A versioned, immutable set of extraction strategies for one source. The schema enforces IR-03's mitigation structurally: every required field declares at least two strategies of DIFFERENT kinds, and none may rely on `css` alone. A single-strategy required field is a single point of failure, and a css-only one is a single point of failure that breaks on the next redesign.

containers.description: Where the reviews are, before which fields they have. `review_node` is required by TR-EXT-030: nodes are located inside the resolved surface, because a document-wide query risks matching similar cards elsewhere on the page. `reply_node` is what EDR-016 detaches first.

rating_stars.description: Parser P2 of the cascade (EDR-017). Not a field entry because it is not a strategy list: it is a pair of selectors whose element COUNTS are compared. Requires the pack to distinguish filled indicators from unfilled ones — a pack that cannot reports five stars for every review.

total_selector.description: All indicators. A five-star widget has exactly five; any other count means the selector matched something that is not the rating widget.

truncation_markers.description: Locale-aware truncation markers (TR-EXT-060). Data, never hard-coded: an English-only marker fails on every other locale by KEEPING the marker, so the published review ends with the word 'More'.

signals.description: Structural signals: challenge pages, empty states, consent interstitials. `empty_state` is load-bearing — it is the only thing separating a listing with genuinely zero reviews from a listing whose markup changed, and those two have opposite correct responses (§21.9).

detectors.description: Deprecated alias for `signals`, retained so v1 keeps validating. Packs at v2 and above use `signals`.

version.description: Packs are immutable once merged; a change is a new version (SEL-01).

min_engine_version.description: Refused if the running engine is older (TR-SEL-031). A pack using a capability the engine lacks fails at load rather than mid-harvest.

notes.description: Pack-level context, including any recorded technical debt (TR-SEL-012).

required.description: A required field with no surviving strategy quarantines the record rather than publishing a null.

strategies.description: Ordered by stability, most stable first. A new strategy is inserted at its correct rank, never appended for convenience (TR-SEL-012).
TR-SEL-010: at least two strategies for a required field.

kind.description: In preference order. `role` and `aria-label-pattern` are highest because accessibility semantics are user-facing contracts: changing them breaks screen readers, so vendors change them rarely. `css` is lowest — fastest to write, first to break.

attribute.description: Read this attribute rather than the text content.

pattern.description: Extract the first capture group from the matched text.

notes.description: REQUIRED (TR-SEL-013). What this targets and why it is ranked here. Six months later nobody remembers why strategy 2 exists, and a pack of undocumented selectors cannot be safely edited by anyone who did not write it.
